premises.name: Module.End.maxGenEigenspaceIndex
premises.type: {R : Type v} {M : Type w} [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] (f : Module.End R M) (μ : R) : ℕ
premises.doc:
If there exists a natural number `k` such that the kernel of `(f - μ • id) ^ k` is the
maximal generalized eigenspace, then this value is the least such `k`. If not, this value is not
meaningful.

premises.name: Module.End.maxUnifEigenspaceIndex

premises.doc:
If there exists a natural number `k` such that the kernel of `(f - μ • id) ^ k` is the

meaningful.

premises.name: Module.End.eigenspace
premises.type: {R : Type v} {M : Type w} [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] (f : Module.End R M) (μ : R) : Submodule R M
premises.doc:
The submodule `eigenspace f μ` for a linear map `f` and a scalar `μ` consists of all vectors `x`
such that `f x = μ • x`. (Def 5.52 of [axler2024]).

premises.name: Module.End.maxGenEigenspace
premises.type: {R : Type v} {M : Type w} [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] (f : Module.End R M) (μ : R) : Submodule R M
premises.doc: The union of the kernels of `(f - μ • id) ^ k` over all `k`.

premises.name: Module.End.maxUnifEigenspaceIndex_le_finrank
premises.type: {K : Type v} {V : Type w} [Field K] [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] [FiniteDimensional K V] (f : Module.End K V) (μ : K) : f.maxUnifEigenspaceIndex μ ≤ Module.finrank K V

premises.name: Module.End.genEigenspace
premises.type: {R : Type v} {M : Type w} [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] (f : Module.End R M) (μ : R) : ℕ∞ →o Submodule R M
premises.doc:
The submodule `genEigenspace f μ k` for a linear map `f`, a scalar `μ`,
and a number `k : ℕ∞` is the kernel of `(f - μ • id) ^ k` if `k` is a natural number,
or the union of all these kernels if `k = ∞`. (`k = ∞` corresponds to Def 8.19 of [axler2024].)
A generalized eigenspace for some exponent `k` is contained in
the generalized eigenspace for exponents larger than `k`.

premises.name: Module.End.eigenspaces_iSupIndep
premises.type: {R : Type v} {M : Type w} [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [IsDomain R] [Module.IsTorsionFree R M] (f : Module.End R M) : iSupIndep f.eigenspace
premises.doc:
The eigenspaces of a linear operator form an independent family of subspaces of `M`.  That is,
any eigenspace has trivial intersection with the span of all the other eigenspaces.

premises.name: Module.End.eigenspace_restrict_le_eigenspace
premises.type: {R : Type v} {M : Type w} [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] (f : Module.End R M) {p : Submodule R M} (hfp : ∀ x ∈ p, f x ∈ p) (μ : R) : Submodule.map p.subtype (Module.End.eigenspace (LinearMap.restrict f hfp) μ) ≤ f.eigenspace μ
premises.doc:
If `p` is an invariant submodule of an endomorphism `f`, then the `μ`-eigenspace of the
restriction of `f` to `p` is a submodule of the `μ`-eigenspace of `f`.

premises.type: {R : Type v} {M : Type w} [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] {f : Module.End R M} {p : Submodule R M} (hfp : ∀ x ∈ p, f x ∈ p) {μ : R} (hμp : Disjoint (f.eigenspace μ) p) : Module.End.eigenspace (LinearMap.restrict f hfp) μ = ⊥
premises.doc:
If an invariant subspace `p` of an endomorphism `f` is disjoint from the `μ`-eigenspace of `f`,
then the restriction of `f` to `p` has trivial `μ`-eigenspace.
